standard_prerequisites.use: Geometric irreducibility and geometric reducedness of fibres, separable finitely generated field extensions with a transcendence basis, and the birational common-open lemma for schemes with isomorphic fraction fields; these are cited inputs, while the model construction in the retained span is the author's own.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where the generic fibre is geometrically reduced as well as geometrically irreducible, using the diagram from the reduced-generic-fibre lemma and the base-change lemma for geometrically irreducible fibres, and assume the base is the spectrum of a domain.

Choose the generic point of the geometrically irreducible and reduced generic fibre, identify its residue field as a separable finitely generated extension with a transcendence basis, and form the minimal polynomial of the last generator.

Build the model algebra B' = A[x_1,...,x_{r+1}]/(P(x_{r+1})), note the polynomial stays irreducible over the algebraic closure, and produce the common dense opens U of X and U' of X' that are isomorphic over the base.
Shrink the base once so that the dense opens stay fibre-wise dense for every base point, and conclude by applying the irreducible-polynomial-over-domain lemma to the model.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to a geometrically reduced generic fibre over a domain, using the reduction diagram and the base-change lemma for geometrically irreducible fibres.
Extract the field-theoretic input: separability, a transcendence basis, and the minimal polynomial of the last generator.
Build the model algebra and the birational isomorphism on common dense opens.
Shrink the base for fibre-wise density and conclude via the irreducible-polynomial-over-domain lemma.

difficulty_reason: Given a finite type morphism of schemes whose generic fibre over the generic point of an irreducible base is geometrically irreducible, one must produce a single nonempty open of the base over which every fibre is geometrically irreducible. The retained first proof is constructive: it first shrinks so the generic fibre is geometrically reduced, then builds an explicit finite type model B' = A[x_1,...,x_{r+1}]/(P) of the generic point from a separating transcendence basis and the minimal polynomial, compares the original scheme and the model on common dense opens, and finishes by a density shrinking argument. The model construction and the birational comparison are the load-bearing steps, and the author states a second independent proof, showing the result is not routine. Retained author proof at lines 7569-7641.
